"'''Jessie's Girl'''" is a song written and performed by Australian singer [[Rick Springfield]]. It was released on the album ''[[Working Class Dog]]'', which was released on January 30, 1981.<ref>{{cite magazine|first= Dave |last= Ling |title= The real story behind Rick Springfield's Jessie's Girl |magazine= [[Classic Rock (magazine)|Classic Rock]] |date= 16 April 2015 |access-date= 24 January 2020 |url= https://www.loudersound.com/features/the-stories-behind-the-songs-rick-springfield-jessie-s-girl}}</ref> The song is about [[unrequited love]] of a young man for his good friend's girlfriend.

Upon its release in the United States in [[1981 in music|1981]], "Jessie's Girl" was slow to break out. It debuted on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] chart on 28 March<ref name="Whitburn">{{cite book|first= Joel |last= Whitburn |author-link= Joel Whitburn |year= 1991 |title= Joel Whitburn's Top Pop Singles 1955–1990 |publisher= Record Research Inc |location= Menomonee Falls, Wisconsin |page= 545}}</ref> but took 19 weeks to hit No. 1<ref name="Grein">{{cite magazine|first= Paul |last= Grein |title= Chartbeat |magazine= Billboard |date= 8 May 1982 |volume= 94 |issue= 18 |page= 6 |issn= 0006-2510 |url= https://books.google.com/books?id=hyQEAAAAMBAJ&pg=PT2}}</ref> reaching that position on 1 August,<ref>{{cite magazine|title= Billboard Hot 100 |magazine= Billboard |date= 1 August 1981 |volume= 93 |issue= 30 |page= 68 |issn= 0006-2510 |url= https://books.google.com/books?id=ASQEAAAAMBAJ&pg=PT67}}</ref> one of the slowest climbs to No. 1 at that time.<ref name="Grein"/> It remained in that position for two weeks and would be Springfield's only No. 1 hit.<ref name="Whitburn"/> The song was at No. 1 when [[MTV]] launched on 1 August 1981.<ref name="Songfacts">{{cite web|title= Jessie's Girl by Rick Springfield |website= Songfacts |access-date= 4 May 2014 |url= http://www.songfacts.com/detail.php?id=3590}}</ref> The song ultimately spent 32 weeks on the chart.<ref>{{cite magazine|title= Rick Springfield – Jessie's Girl – Chart History |magazine= [[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |access-date= 11 May 2018 |url= https://www.billboard.com/artist/rick-springfield/chart-history/hsi/}}</ref> ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' ranked it as No. 5 for all of 1981.<ref name="US"/>

The song also peaked at No. 1 in Springfield's native country of [[Australia]] and later won him a [[Grammy Award for Best Male Rock Vocal Performance]] at the [[24th Annual Grammy Awards]].

"Jessie's Girl" was released in the United Kingdom in March 1984 and peaked at No. 43 on the [[UK Singles Chart]] in April 1984.<ref name="UK"/>

''[[Record World]]'' said that "a strong rhythm guitar fuels the [[Pop rock|pop-rocker]] while Rick's determined vocal works the hook."<ref name=rw>{{cite magazine|magazine=Record World|date=March 21, 1981|page=12|accessdate=2023-02-26|title=Single Picks|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Record-World/80s/81/RW-1981-03-21.pdf}}</ref>

Springfield recorded an acoustic version of the song for his 1999 album, ''[[Karma (Rick Springfield album)|Karma]]''.

"Jessie's Girl" is a song written and performed by Australian singer Rick Springfield. It was released on the album Working Class Dog, which was released on January 30, 1981. The song is about unrequited love of a young man for his good friend's girlfriend.

Upon its release in the United States in 1981, "Jessie's Girl" was slow to break out. It debuted on the Billboard Hot 100 chart on 28 March but took 19 weeks to hit No. 1 reaching that position on 1 August, one of the slowest climbs to No. 1 at that time. It remained in that position for two weeks and would be Springfield's only No. 1 hit. The song was at No. 1 when MTV launched on 1 August 1981. The song ultimately spent 32 weeks on the chart. Billboard ranked it as No. 5 for all of 1981.

The song also peaked at No. 1 in Springfield's native country of Australia and later won him a Grammy Award for Best Male Rock Vocal Performance at the 24th Annual Grammy Awards.

"Jessie's Girl" was released in the United Kingdom in March 1984 and peaked at No. 43 on the UK Singles Chart in April 1984.

Record World said that "a strong rhythm guitar fuels the pop-rocker while Rick's determined vocal works the hook."

Springfield recorded an acoustic version of the song for his 1999 album, Karma.

sections.heading: Background
sections.wikitext:
In the late 1970s, Rick Springfield took a [[stained glass]] class in [[Pasadena, California|Pasadena]]. Also in the class was a man named Gary as well as Gary's girlfriend. Springfield became friends with both, while developing feelings for the girlfriend. He wrote the song based on the negative feelings he had about the situation. Springfield initially wanted to use the actual name of his friend, but decided to go with a different name as "Gary" didn't sound good when being sung. He chose "Jessie" because he was wearing a T-shirt with the name of football player [[Ron Jessie]] on it.<ref>{{cite magazine|title= "Jessie's Girl" cracks the Top 40 |magazine= [[Entertainment Weekly]] |date= 7 May 1999 |access-date= 4 May 2014 |url= https://ew.com/article/1999/05/07/jessies-girl-cracks-top-40/}}</ref><ref name="Songfacts" />

Springfield says that he does not remember the name of the girlfriend, and he believes that the real woman who inspired the song has no idea that she was "Jessie's Girl". He told [[Oprah Winfrey]], "I was never really introduced to her. It was always just, like, panting from afar."<ref>{{cite web|title= Is Rick Springfield Jessie's Girl a Real Person? |publisher= [[The Oprah Winfrey Show]] |url= http://www2.oprah.com/tows/slide/200802/20080226/slide_20080226_350_103.jhtml |archive-date= 6 July 2008 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20080706200642/http://www2.oprah.com/tows/slide/200802/20080226/slide_20080226_350_103.jhtml}}</ref> Springfield told [[Songfacts]] that Winfrey's people had tried to find her, and they got as far back as finding out that the teacher of the class had died two years previously and that his class records were thrown out one year after his death.<ref name="Songfacts"/> In 2006, the song was named No. 20 on [[VH1]]'s "100 Greatest Songs of the 80s".<ref>{{cite web|title= 100 Greatest Songs of the 80's: #1 –100 |publisher= [[VH1 Classic]] |url= http://www.vh1classic.com/view/playlist/1553683/59441/100_Greatest_Songs_of_The_80_s_1_100/Jessie_s_Girl/index.jhtml |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20090722172607/http://www.vh1classic.com/view/playlist/1553683/59441/100_Greatest_Songs_of_The_80_s_1_100/Jessie_s_Girl/index.jhtml |archive-date= 22 July 2009}}</ref>
sections.text:
In the late 1970s, Rick Springfield took a stained glass class in Pasadena. Also in the class was a man named Gary as well as Gary's girlfriend. Springfield became friends with both, while developing feelings for the girlfriend. He wrote the song based on the negative feelings he had about the situation. Springfield initially wanted to use the actual name of his friend, but decided to go with a different name as "Gary" didn't sound good when being sung. He chose "Jessie" because he was wearing a T-shirt with the name of football player Ron Jessie on it.

Springfield says that he does not remember the name of the girlfriend, and he believes that the real woman who inspired the song has no idea that she was "Jessie's Girl". He told Oprah Winfrey, "I was never really introduced to her. It was always just, like, panting from afar." Springfield told Songfacts that Winfrey's people had tried to find her, and they got as far back as finding out that the teacher of the class had died two years previously and that his class records were thrown out one year after his death. In 2006, the song was named No. 20 on VH1's "100 Greatest Songs of the 80s".

sections.heading: Certifications
Coheed and Cambria sequel
sections.wikitext:
On 21 August 2020, the American [[progressive rock]] band [[Coheed and Cambria]] released a music video entitled "Jessie's Girl 2" to their official [[YouTube]] channel.<ref>{{cite news|first= Josh |last= Johnson |title= Coheed and Cambria continues the story of "Jessie's Girl" with new song, "Jessie's Girl 2" |publisher= [[ABC News Radio]] |date= 21 August 2020 |access-date= 29 August 2020 |url= http://abcnewsradioonline.com/music-news/2020/8/21/coheed-and-cambria-continues-the-story-of-jessies-girl-with.html}}</ref> The video depicts Springfield, who supplies some of the song's vocals, working in a bar while the titular "Jessie's Girl" wreaks havoc. The lyrics state that the protagonist from the original song was successful in stealing the Girl away from Jessie, but realizes that she is mentally unstable. The protagonist muses that he was likely set up by Jessie, in order for him to be rid of the woman,<ref>{{cite web|last=Rea|first=Carla|title= Jessie's Girl 2: He Got Jessie's Girl - But There's a Twist |publisher= 96.3 KKLZ |date= 24 August 2020 |access-date= 27 August 2020 |url= https://963kklz.com/2020/08/24/jessies-girl-2-he-got-jessies-girl-but-theres-a-twist/}}</ref> and that he (the protagonist) is now trapped in a loveless marriage with children and a future he did not want. The video ends with the Girl stealing the barkeeper's keys and escaping.<ref name="EW">{{cite magazine|first= Maureen Lee |last= Lenker |title= Exclusive: Rick Springfield's 'Jessie's Girl' gets murderous sequel in Coheed and Cambria music video |magazine= [[Entertainment Weekly]] |date= 21 August 2020 |access-date= 27 August 2020 |url= https://ew.com/music/exclusive-rick-springfield-jessies-girl-sequel-song-coheed-and-cambria-video/}}</ref> The song also references [[Tommy Tutone]]'s "[[867-5309/Jenny]]" via lyrics that mention the protagonist changing his number.<ref name="EW"/>

The band's frontman, Claudio Sanchez, stated that the song is "kind of like a ''[[National Lampoon (magazine)|National Lampoon’s]]'' movie meets ''[[So I Married an Axe Murderer]]''."<ref name="CoS">{{cite web|first= Spencer |last= Kaufman |title= Coheed and Cambria unleash "Jessie's Girl 2" featuring Rick Springfield: Stream |website= [[Consequence of Sound]] |date= 21 August 2020 |access-date= 27 August 2020 |url= https://consequenceofsound.net/2020/08/coheed-and-cambria-jessies-girl-2-rick-springfield/}}</ref> Sanchez had originally come up with the idea of a sequel during a 2019 studio session and later approached Springfield to pitch the idea via an [[Instagram|Instagram Live]] session.<ref>{{cite web|first= Chad |last= Childers |title= Coheed & Cambria Give Rick Springfield's 'Jessie's Girl' a Sequel |website= [[Loudwire]] |date= 21 August 2020 |access-date= 27 August 2020 |url= https://loudwire.com/coheed-and-cambria-rick-springfield-jessies-girl-2-sequel/}}</ref> Springfield liked the draft prepared by Coheed and Cambria and agreed to participate.<ref>{{cite magazine|first= Katherine |last= Turman |title= Coheed and Cambria Share 'Jessie's Girl 2' Video Featuring Rick Springfield |magazine= [[Spin (magazine)|Spin]] |date= 21 August 2020 |access-date= 27 August 2020 |url= https://www.spin.com/2020/08/coheed-and-cambria-share-jessies-girl-2-video-featuring-rick-springfield/}}</ref>

Coheed and Cambria released the single digitally and as a [[Single (music)|7-inch single]] in September 2020.<ref name="CoS"/>
sections.text:
On 21 August 2020, the American progressive rock band Coheed and Cambria released a music video entitled "Jessie's Girl 2" to their official YouTube channel. The video depicts Springfield, who supplies some of the song's vocals, working in a bar while the titular "Jessie's Girl" wreaks havoc. The lyrics state that the protagonist from the original song was successful in stealing the Girl away from Jessie, but realizes that she is mentally unstable. The protagonist muses that he was likely set up by Jessie, in order for him to be rid of the woman, and that he (the protagonist) is now trapped in a loveless marriage with children and a future he did not want. The video ends with the Girl stealing the barkeeper's keys and escaping. The song also references Tommy Tutone's "867-5309/Jenny" via lyrics that mention the protagonist changing his number.

The band's frontman, Claudio Sanchez, stated that the song is "kind of like a National Lampoon’s movie meets So I Married an Axe Murderer." Sanchez had originally come up with the idea of a sequel during a 2019 studio session and later approached Springfield to pitch the idea via an Instagram Live session. Springfield liked the draft prepared by Coheed and Cambria and agreed to participate.

Coheed and Cambria released the single digitally and as a 7-inch single in September 2020.

sections.heading: In popular culture
sections.wikitext:
In regards to the song's use in films such as ''[[Boogie Nights]]'' and ''[[13 Going on 30]]'' over 20 years after its original release, Springfield said, "I'm thrilled by it. As a writer, all you can ask is that a song has legs. It has an appeal that keeps coming back."<ref>{{cite news |first= Heather |last= Murtagh |title= Are you ready to rock?: '80s legend Rick Springfield to perform at county fair |newspaper= [[San Mateo Daily Journal|The Daily Journal]] |date= 18 June 2010 |access-date= 4 May 2014 |url= http://archives.smdailyjournal.com/article_preview.php?id=133965 |archive-date= 4 May 2014 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20140504035830/http://archives.smdailyjournal.com/article_preview.php?id=133965 |url-status= dead }}</ref>

In 2010, ''Jessie's Girl'' was covered on ''[[Glee (TV series)|Glee]]'' in the episode ''[[Laryngitis (Glee)|Laryngitis]]''. In the same year, the cover was certified gold by the [[Australian Recording Industry Association]].<ref>{{cite web|title= ARIA Charts – Accreditations – 2010 Singles |publisher= [[Australian Recording Industry Association]] |url= http://www.aria.com.au/pages/httpwww.aria.com.auaccreds2010.htm |access-date= 6 August 2010}}</ref>

In 2010, Jessie's Girl was covered on Glee in the episode Laryngitis. In the same year, the cover was certified gold by the Australian Recording Industry Association.
